strengths: Highly practical motivation: The paper successfully shifts the text-to-CAD paradigm from static one-shot generation to a dynamic, proactive interactive loop, which is critical since real-world engineering descriptions are naturally prone to under-specification or contradiction.

Excellent data curation pipeline: By combining CadQuery representations with multi-view visual renders, and incorporating a verification loop with data-leakage and completeness checks, the paper produces a high-quality dataset of 10K clean samples.
Impressive data efficiency: Fine-tuning a Qwen-2.5-7B model on only 1.6K samples (ProCAD-coder) yields performance competitive with or superior to Claude 4.5 Sonnet on unambiguous text-to-CAD tasks.

Rigorous and multi-faceted evaluation: The evaluation covers both simulated closed-loop interactions (generalizing to OOD user models like Claude 4.5 Haiku) and expert human-centered evaluations on real human-written ambiguous prompts.
Exceptional presentation and ablation studies: The paper is beautifully written, with extensive qualitative examples, clear failure analyses, and deep protocol ablations in the appendix.
weaknesses: Dependence on frontier vision-language models: The automated data curation and user-simulation pipelines depend heavily on high-end APIs (e.g., GPT-5-mini, Claude 4.5 Sonnet), which could pose access barriers for open-source reproduction.

Scope of CAD geometry: The dataset is built on the DeepCAD base, which mainly covers relatively simple mechanical primitives and extrusions. It remains unclear how well the proactive clarifier scales to complex 3D assemblies or freeform surfaces.

Simplistic modeling of user responses: The study assumes a cooperative, precise user who always provides exact numbers when asked. Real-world users may provide vague, qualitative answers to clarification questions, which could complicate the multi-round trajectory.

strengths: The proactive clarifying agent framework (ProCAD) is highly practical and elegantly addresses a fundamental limitation in text-to-CAD generation, where user inputs are often under-specified or contradictory.

The data annotation pipeline is exceptionally rigorous, incorporating multi-view image rendering, code leakage checks, and a 'generate-then-verify' completeness check via actual execution and Chamfer distance calculations.

The proposed method shows remarkable performance. Fine-tuning a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model on just 1.6K clean samples outperforms giant frontier models like Claude 4.5 Sonnet on both code validity and geometric accuracy.

The evaluation is highly comprehensive, spanning automated LLM-based user simulations (under different model backbones for out-of-distribution robustness), real human-centered evaluations, and a thorough interaction protocol ablation.
weaknesses: The paper frequently references and utilizes 'GPT-5-mini' (citing Singh et al., 2025/2026) for dataset curation and evaluation. As this model may not be universally accessible or publicly available, it poses potential concerns for exact reproducibility of the dataset generation pipeline.

The vocabulary of ambiguity is somewhat limited, focusing primarily on missing dimensions or conflicting numeric values. Real-world human ambiguities can often be structural or semantic (e.g., ambiguous spatial relationships, vague shape terminologies), which are not fully addressed in the current perturbation scheme.

The underlying CAD code relies on reconstructed programs from Rukhovich et al. (2025), meaning any systematic reconstruction biases or limitations in supported CAD commands (e.g., complex sweeps, lofting, or draft angles) from the source dataset will carry over to ProCAD.

strengths: Identifies and addresses a critical, real-world bottleneck in Text-to-CAD systems: the fact that natural language user prompts are often under-specified, ambiguous, or internally inconsistent.

Proposes a well-designed, modular two-agent framework (ProCAD) consisting of a proactive clarifier and a CAD coder, effectively separating geometric reasoning/dialogue from syntax-heavy code generation.
Develops a rigorous, semi-automatic data creation pipeline that leverages visual and symbolic signals alongside code-leakage and completeness checks to curate a high-quality text-to-CadQuery dataset.

Achieves exceptional performance with extremely lightweight fine-tuning (only 1.6K samples for the coder), significantly outperforming frontier closed-source models like Claude Sonnet 4.5 on downstream invalidity ratio and Chamfer distance.
Includes a comprehensive suite of evaluations, including out-of-distribution user simulator testing, ablation studies on interaction protocols, and human-centered evaluations with CAD experts.
weaknesses: The underlying geometric dataset is limited to DeepCAD, which contains relatively simple, single-body mechanical components. The effectiveness of the proactive agentic framework on highly complex, multi-part assemblies with complex inter-part constraints remains unverified.

The training and evaluation of the clarifying agent rely heavily on simulated user responses generated by frontier LLMs. While validated by a small-scale human check, simulated users tend to be more cooperative, logical, and structured than real-world designers, who may struggle to articulate dimensions even when prompted.

The data curation and verification pipeline heavily relies on access to proprietary frontier models (e.g., GPT-5-mini), which may restrict the immediate reproducibility and adaptability of the pipeline for academic researchers with limited resource access.
